summary: Private helper providing GzipCompressingReader, a RawIOBase adapter that lazily produces an RFC 1952 gzip member (header, raw deflate, CRC32/size trailer) as the consumer reads, so Gzip.wrap can compress a stream without draining it. A fixed mtime (default 0) yields byte-identical output for identical input.
key_classes: GzipCompressingReader — read-side lazy gzip encoder over a source BinaryIO (level, mtime, chunk_size=64 KiB)
key_functions: _gzip_header(mtime) -> bytes — minimal RFC 1952 header with OS=unknown and no flags
extension_points: None; pattern (RawIOBase reader that fills an internal buffer from a codec) is the template for future streaming encoders
lifecycle_notes: Construction reads nothing from the source; the first fill emits the header and compresses the first chunk.
close() closes the wrapped source, then itself.
Uses zlib.compressobj with -MAX_WBITS (raw deflate); CRC and size are tracked modulo 2**32 per RFC 1952.
documentation_hooks: Maintainer note: gzip write-path laziness and reproducibility (mtime=0)
Contributor template for adding a streaming encoder
risks: close() closes the source stream it was given, contradicting the read-side convention that transforms leave borrowed inputs open (docs/read-access-modes.md); a caller passing its own file to Gzip.wrap will find it closed.
No direct unit tests; coverage is indirect through Gzip tests (lazy wrap, reproducibility, round trip).
readinto lacks a type annotation, inconsistent with the 'annotate all functions' code-style rule in AGENTS.md.
open_questions: Is the source-closing behaviour of GzipCompressingReader.close() intentional for the write path?

evidence.detail: Only consumer: Gzip.wrap returns GzipCompressingReader(stream, level, mtime)
test_gzip_wrap_is_lazy and test_gzip_mtime_zero_is_reproducible exercise the encoder indirectly
